title: The Damon Runyon Theatre
paragraphs: Radio adaptations of Damon Runyon's Broadway stories, narrated by the character 'Broadway' and populated by gamblers, gangsters, show people, dreamers, and other colorful figures of Runyon's New York.

Syndicated anthology dramatizing 52 Damon Runyon short stories. Story numbers 1-52 are stable, while two documented market/distribution schedules place the same numbered programs about thirteen weeks apart. GRH freezes the Jan-Dec 1949 schedule.
GRH documents the program through Earlier syndication schedule (October 3, 1948 to September 25, 1949) and Later syndication schedule (January 2, 1949 to December 25, 1949).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Damon Runyon (author on 52 recordings), [[person|john-brown|John Brown]] (performer on 52 recordings), Richard Sanville (director on 52 recordings), Russell Hughes (radio adaptor on 49 recordings and writer on 5 recordings), Vern Carstensen (production supervisor on 52 recordings and performer on 8 recordings), Frank Gallop (announcer on 51 recordings), and [[person|jeff-chandler|Jeff Chandler]] (performer on 5 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.c76079baded29531|Mayfair]] (syndicated by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Broadway and New York nightlife, show business and performers, romance and courtship, loyalty, friendship and obligation, gangsters and criminal underworld, and horse racing and racetrack culture.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar transcription syndication, Posthumous adaptation of Damon Runyon stories, Runyonesque Broadway vernacular on radio, and Independent Hollywood-star production.
